messages:
eli: quick sync — i'm trying to land a change for how we flush mmap'ed host-staging pages under high-churn workloads. proposal: introduce a small 'staged flush window' + optional io-throttling token to smooth spikes. pinging runtime folks for tradeoffs.

maya: curious — what's the primary problem we're seeing today? spikes in host io causing eviction stalls?

eli: exactly. on models with lots of short-lived KV cache entries we see IO bursts that make the eviction path block longer, which in turn spikes latency for in-flight tokens.

thomas: high-level question: is this about batching flushes to avoid many small writes, or about rate-limiting concurrent flushes? they feel related but different.

eli: both. i think we can fold them: accumulate flushable segments for X ms (the window), then drain them with a concurrency cap. window avoids tiny writes, cap avoids IO saturation.

nina: downside: increases time-to-evict for items that become hot again in the window. could hurt tail latency for some requests.

maya: do we have data to quantify that hit? if the window is like 5–10ms maybe okay; if 50–100ms that could be bad.

eli: preliminary traces show median extra residency ~6ms, p95 ~28ms for a 10ms window in our dev rig. but io timeouts collapse with less queueing.

alex: implementation thought: allocator would mark segments as "flushable" and push to a flush queue. flush workers pop up to N concurrent tasks. we surface an API to the allocator to query "is_flush_backed_up()" so eviction can decide to either stall or pick another victim.

sam: can we avoid allocator-level stalling by letting eviction fallback to compressed-on-host pages or a local RAM staging lane? more complexity though.

thomas: also think about ordering: if GPU has a pending migration, we must ensure flush of pages for that region happens immediately. urgent flushes should bypass window.

eli: yes — plan includes an "urgent" flag that skips batching and increments a priority counter; urgent flushes still subject to global concurrency cap to prevent total IO overload.

nina: about the backpressure API — what shape? something like: allocator.pause_io(token) / resume_io(token) or a leaky-bucket token-bucket rate limit?

eli: sketched API:
```
// runtime flush controller
struct FlushController {
  set_window_ms(u32);
  set_concurrency(u16);
  throttle_rate(bytes_per_sec);
  mark_urgent(segment_id);
  is_backed_up() -> bool;
}
```
eviction path uses is_backed_up() to decide fallback behavior.

maya: love the explicit knobs. two questions: (1) who owns these settings? per-node or per-tenant? (2) how do we expose them in Dedicated/Hosted?

eli: defaults global per-node, but we can let tenants override via config on Dedicated. Hosted initially only global; we'll add per-tenant controls later.

alex: ops concern: we need metrics + events: flush_queue_length, avg_flush_batch_size, flush_latency_p50/p95, io_backpressure_active boolean. Also tracing annotations when eviction chooses fallback due to backpressure.

thomas: add a safety: if backpressure persists > T seconds, trigger an emergency GC that increases eviction aggressiveness or degrades QoS for low-tier requests.

nina: edge-case: what if urgent flush + concurrency cap cause priority inversion? urgent flushes join queue front but if there are many urgent requests from a rogue tenant they could starve normals. need per-tenant fairness.

eli: good call. we'll introduce per-tenant concurrency shares and an emergency override that requires operator confirmation.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: CI check started for branch "staged-flush-window" (build #4521). Status: running :gear:

maya: implementation detail: where do we track segments for batching? in the allocator metadata (cheap) or a separate flush-index? allocator already knows live/dirty bits so add a small list of candidates seems easiest.

thomas: but be careful with locks. we don't want hot-path allocator ops to take global locks for flush list. maybe a lock-free MPSC queue per arena.

eli: agreed — per-arena MPSC queue + background flush worker pool. workers take snapshot of items every window tick.

alex: testing plan: synthetic workload that alloc/frees small KV regions at various churn rates, measure latency, IO throughput, and stability. also chaos test where we force disk slowdown and observe backpressure behavior.

sam: i'm worried about complexity surface for Private customers who manage their own KMS and storage — need clear docs on knobs and safe defaults.

eli: will document defaults and recommended overrides. aim to keep defaults conservative.

maya: one more perf thought: if we batch by physical adjacency we can combine writes into larger contiguous IOs. does allocator maintain physical adjacency info?

eli: we do—arena segments are contiguous by design for staging. flush worker will attempt coalescing adjacent segments into a single write when possible.

nina: +1 on coalescing, that should reduce IOPS significantly. but maintain max-coalesce-size to avoid giant writes.

thomas: do we need a feature flag for rollout? canary first in a small fleet, watch flush metrics and tail latency.

eli: yes will ship behind feature flag and enable for canary group. rollout plan: canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h if no regressions.

alex: please add a health-signal for console: "flush-backpressure" that'll show up on per-node dashboard. ops can auto-scale or remove node if active.

eli: action items: (1) i'll open RFC PR with the API sketch + perf numbers (2) thomas will prototype per-arena MPSC queue (3) alex will draft metrics + dashboard panels (4) maya/nina will design test harness.

sam: ack. thanks all.

infra-bot: CI build #4521 passed :white_check_mark: (tests: 432/432)

eli: sweet, i'll start the RFC PR and link here. thanks for quick feedback :rocket:
